images.title: An isosceles triangle folded in half
images.purpose: Show the concept's own triangle with sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm: its 2 equal sides, and the fold that makes the two halves match so that its 2 base angles are equal.
images.composition: Two panels. On the left the triangle with its sides labelled and the 2 equal sides ticked; on the right the same triangle folded in half along a dashed line, one half teal and one half amber, with matching arcs at the 2 base corners.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, two panels side by side, drawn to scale (80 px for every 1 cm). PANEL HEADINGS: the text Isosceles triangle centred at (380,100) and the text Folded in half centred at (1076,100), both bold dark #1F2937 sans-serif, 44 px. LEFT PANEL, exactly 1 triangle with corners (260,610), (500,610) and (380,228) (base 240 px wide, height 382 px, each of the two long sides about 400 px), filled teal #0072B2 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px). On each of the 2 long sides exactly 1 equal-sides tick: a short straight line, reddish purple #CC79A7, 5 px thick, 32 px long, crossing the side at its middle: on the left side from (335,424) to (305,414) and on the right side from (425,424) to (455,414). Side labels in bold dark text, 34 px: 5 cm centred at (278,406) outside the left long side, 5 cm centred at (482,406) outside the right long side, and 3 cm centred at (380,652) under the base. Under the triangle the text 2 equal sides, bold dark, 44 px, centred at (380,715). RIGHT PANEL, the same triangle shifted right, with corners (956,610), (1196,610) and (1076,228), outline dark 3 px. A dashed vertical fold line in grey #6B7280 (4 px, dashes 14 px long with 10 px gaps) runs from the top corner (1076,228) straight down to the middle of the base (1076,610). The left half, with corners (956,610), (1076,228) and (1076,610), is filled teal #0072B2; the right half, with corners (1076,228), (1196,610) and (1076,610), is filled amber #E69F00. At each of the 2 base corners exactly 1 small white arc (5 px thick, radius 56 px) is drawn inside the triangle, from the base to the long side, one at (956,610) and one at (1196,610). Exactly 1 curved arrow in grey #6B7280, 5 px thick, arches over the top corner from (1026,200) up to a peak at (1076,140) and down to (1126,200), with its small arrowhead at the right end. Under the right triangle the text 2 equal angles, bold dark, 44 px, centred at (1076,715), and under it the text The two halves match, dark, 34 px, centred at (1076,765). There are no other ticks, arcs, arrows or marks. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any number written on an angle, and any angle-measuring tool, anywhere in the frame
any shape drawn out of proportion to the stated side lengths
more or fewer than 2 ticks, 2 arcs or 1 arrow
a triangle whose 2 long sides are visibly different in length
any label on the fold line
images.takeaway: A triangle with 2 equal sides, 5 cm and 5 cm, folds in half so that the two halves match, which shows that it also has 2 equal angles.
images.description: A triangle with sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm, with its 2 equal sides ticked, and the same triangle folded in half with its 2 base angles marked equal.
images.context: Concept image for Isosceles Triangles. It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (a triangle with 2 equal sides, folded in half to compare its angles) and shows the concept's own example of sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm.
images.teaching_notes: Let the child fold a paper triangle in half along the same line. The slip to watch is thinking that only the sides of an isosceles triangle are equal: the fold shows that the 2 angles at the ends of the third side match as well.

image_decisions.why: The triangle with its 2 ticked sides and the dashed fold line show that equal sides and equal angles come as a pair, which words alone do not show.
